title: Intelligent quantization path selector and prefill/decode orchestration to minimize dequant overhead
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Goal: Reduce end-to-end per-token cost and tail latency by selecting a quantization-aware kernel path at request time and by reworking prefill + decode scheduling to avoid repeated dequantization. Scope covers kernel registry policy changes, small-batch decode fast-paths, tiled/fused attention adaptations for INT8/FP8, and runtime orchestration that overlaps dequant work with I/O and KV population.

Background: Current serving runtime frequently pays dequantization costs in the critical path, especially for mixed-precision models where prefill uses an INT8-packed storage but decode expects FP16/FP32 buffers. Repeated pack/unpack and nave kernel selection increases GPU kernel launches and memory movement, hurting p99 latency and throughput for low-concurrency workloads (chat use case).

Proposal: Implement an "intelligent quant path selector" (IQPS) that: 1) Maintains a per-model cost profile (tokens/sec, dequant cycles, memory bandwidth) for supported kernel implementations (INT8 fused-attn, FP8 epilogue, mixed FP16 fallback). 2) Estimates request-level accuracy budget (from model metadata + request labels like high-fidelity=true) and chooses the cheapest kernel path that meets accuracy constraints. 3) Applies a scheduling policy that: a) forces eager dequant of prefix tokens for long prefill requests and overlaps that work with KV writes and metrics aggregation; b) for short decode loops (batch size <= 4, seq_len<=128) prefers a requantized streaming path that avoids roundtrip dequant on each step; c) uses attention tiling adjustments for INT8 kernels to reduce warp divergence on long sequences.

Implementation notes: - Kernel registry changes: add attributes {quant_mode, requires_dequant, tiled_attn_reqs, mem_pressure} and expose metrics. - New runtime planner stage that consults the IQPS cost model and current GPU utilization to pick kernel + prefill strategy. - Add a lightweight on-host micro-benchmark (1s harness) to update cost model periodically per device. - Introduce lazy-dequant handles in KV cache: store packed INT8 and expose an on-GPU dequant path fused into the first QKV compute when possible. - Safety: fall back to FP16 if quantized kernel fails accuracy/on-device constraints.

Metrics / acceptance criteria: - End-to-end hosted-chat p50 latency within +5% of baseline while reducing token unit cost by >=15% on 13B/70B quantized families. - Small-batch decode (B<=4) p95 tail latency improved by >=10%. - No regression in model quality (per-eval prompt set) beyond 0.5% delta on LLM QA metrics when using the selected quant path under normal accuracy budget.

Bench plan: run against LLaMA2-13B and an experimental FP8-quantized 13B casted from our compilation pipeline. Benchmarks: 1) synthetic high-concurrency throughput (B=64, seq=512), 2) chat-style small-batch latency (B=1..4, step decode), 3) cold prefill (single long prompt seq=2048). Compare baseline runtime-1.21 fused kernels vs IQPS selections on p4d and A100 pools.

Rollout: feature gated behind runtime-1.22 flag. Start with A/B on canary customers with low QPS, then expand to dedicated pools after 2 weeks stability and perf validation.

Risks / trade-offs: - Cost-model staleness if GPU topology changes; mitigated by periodic micro-benchmarks. - Increased complexity in kernel registry and rollout; mitigated by feature flag and strict fallbacks. - Slightly higher memory usage for maintaining both packed and unpacked representations temporarily; measured in bench plan.
